questions.q: What is the serving layer's job, specifically?
options: Putting gold's business-ready data in front of its actual consumers — dashboards, applications, analysts
Cleaning and deduplicating data arriving from bronze
Deciding whether ingestion should be batch or streaming
Enforcing schema-on-write at the point data first arrives
questions.explain: Getting bronze, silver, and gold right and then serving gold badly still leaves the end user with a slow, wrong, or unusable answer.

questions.q: Why isn't there one universally correct serving layer choice?
options: A warehouse, semantic model, API, and cache each fit different consumers — who's actually querying it, the same deciding factor from Fabric Lesson 11
A cache is always the correct choice regardless of the consumer
Only a data warehouse can ever serve a gold table
Serving layer choice is decided entirely by data volume, never by consumer
questions.explain: An analyst team fits a warehouse; a BI tool fits a semantic model; application code fits an API — matched by who's consuming it.

questions.q: What makes Fabric's Direct Lake mode a genuinely different third option, not a compromise?
options: It reads gold's Delta Parquet files directly, combining Import's speed with DirectQuery's freshness, via Delta's transaction log
It is simply a faster version of DirectQuery with no other differences
It requires copying gold's data into Power BI's own format, like Import mode
It only works with non-Delta file formats
questions.explain: Direct Lake leans on the same transaction log (Databricks Lesson 17) that already made time travel and safe concurrent writes possible.

questions.q: Why should the serving layer be tuned for reads while the transformation layer is tuned for writes?
options: Gold is read many times by many concurrent consumers, while the transformation layer is MERGE-heavy and built for correct repeated writes
The serving layer should always be optimized for writes, matching the transformation layer
Read and write optimization make no practical difference for analytics data
Only the transformation layer needs any performance tuning at all
questions.explain: Optimizing gold for writes it rarely receives, at the expense of the reads it constantly receives, gets the trade-off backward.

questions.q: Why might the same gold table reasonably serve both a T-SQL warehouse and a Direct Lake semantic model at once?
options: Different consumers genuinely need different front doors onto the same underlying gold data — the same mixed pattern Fabric Lesson 11 described
Gold data must always be duplicated into two separate physical tables to do this
A warehouse and a semantic model cannot ever read the same underlying data
This is only possible if the gold table has no partitioning at all
questions.explain: Serving isn't always one choice — an analyst team's ad hoc T-SQL needs and a dashboard's consistent measures can both be met from the same gold tables.
